claim_text: Bell MTS email outage was a cyberattack
summary: Bell MTS told the Free Press on Nov 22 that its third-party email provider confirmed a cyberattack caused the outage. Bell's earlier posts gave no cause. No second outlet has the statement yet.
detail: The Free Press quotes a Bell MTS email statement: the provider confirmed a cyberattack caused password resets, let a "threat actor" into some email accounts and locked out customers from others. We found no Bell MTS notice on its own channels. One company statement, one outlet, so the label stays Reported until a second outlet or Bell's own notice carries it.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The Free Press prints a statement from Bell MTS saying a cyberattack caused the email outage.
notes: Single outlet, single company statement. Counted as one source.

claim_text: Attacker got into some email accounts and locked others out
summary: Per Bell MTS's statement to the Free Press, a threat actor accessed some email accounts and locked out customers from others. Bell says it will follow up directly with customers whose data may have been affected.
detail: Bell MTS did not say how many accounts were accessed or what was in them. The statement says the provider's investigation continues.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The Free Press quotes the statement describing access to some accounts and lockouts of others.

claim_text: Bell MTS customers in Manitoba were locked out of email for days; Bell said it was restored Nov 20
summary: Bell MTS posted on social media on Wed, Nov 18 about an email service interruption, and said around 2:30 PM ET Fri, Nov 20 that service was restored. Many customers still could not log in and were told to reset passwords.
detail: CBC reports customers locked out since Tuesday night or Wednesday morning, more than two days. The Free Press reports customers saying the outage began as early as Monday, Nov 16, and that a follow-up post on Thursday told customers to reset passwords and use webmail. Bell's restoration post said customers might need to reset passwords by self-serve portal or phone. The Free Press says several customers were still locked out after the restoration post.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: CBC and the Free Press each report the Bell MTS posts and customers locked out; both report Bell said service was restored Nov 20.
notes: Two outlets with their own reporting. Customer accounts of the start date vary (Nov 12 to Nov 18).

claim_text: Bell MTS gave no cause until Sunday, Nov 22
summary: Through Friday, Nov 20, Bell MTS would not say what caused the outage or how many customers were affected, per CBC and the Free Press. On Nov 22 it told the Free Press the cause was a cyberattack.
detail: Bell MTS's spokesperson told the Free Press that when it posted about the outage last week, it was working with the information it had at the time, and that the email provider did not initially attribute the outage to a cybersecurity incident.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: CBC and the Free Press each report on Nov 20 that Bell gave no cause; the Nov 22 Free Press story reports Bell later naming a cyberattack.
notes: Plain statement of what Bell did and did not say.

claim_text: A flaw in the password-reset tool was exploited
summary: Bell MTS says the provider that runs its email service found a vulnerability in its password-resetting application was exploited. The provider did not at first treat the outage as a security incident.
detail: The Free Press attributes this to the Bell MTS spokesperson. The provider is not named in the story. No technical detail or fix is described beyond the remediation statement.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The Free Press quotes Bell MTS saying an investigation found the password-reset application vulnerability was exploited.

claim_text: Bell MTS says the incident is fixed and password reset is back on
summary: Bell MTS says the incident has been remediated and online password reset is re-enabled for all customers. The investigation with its provider continues.
detail: Reported only through the Free Press. Whether all locked-out customers have regained access has not been independently checked.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The Free Press quotes the remediation and password-reset statement.

claim_text: How many customers or accounts were affected, and what data
summary: Neither Bell MTS nor any outlet has said how many accounts were accessed or locked out, or what data was in them. Bell says it will contact customers whose data may have been affected.
detail: CBC and the Free Press reported on Nov 20 that Bell MTS would not say how many customers were affected. The Nov 22 statement does not give a number either.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No source gives a count or says what data was reachable.
notes: Needed: a Bell MTS or provider notice with numbers.

summary: Nobody has been named. Bell MTS's statement did not identify the threat actor, and we found no claim of responsibility in press coverage.
detail: We did not look at leak sites, underground forums or trackers.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The Free Press says the spokesperson did not identify the threat actor.

claim_text: This is the same attack as Bell Canada's Nov 17 breach
summary: The Free Press reports Bell's spokesperson calling the Nov 17 Bell Canada intrusion a separate cyberattack. No source says the two share an attacker or entry point.
detail: Bell's own accounts of Nov 17 (to CBC, the Globe and Mail and BleepingComputer) describe an ordering and provisioning system and enterprise customer data. The email outage ran through a third-party provider's password-reset application. The Free Press story says: "On Tuesday, a separate cyberattack also targeted Bell Canada's internal systems." Corrected Nov 25: this row earlier quoted only "also targeted" and called the wording unclear; the story says "separate". On Nov 23 Bell told CBC that Bell MTS customers were among those affected by the Nov 17 incident (c013), which is about customer data, not email.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The Free Press reports Bell calling the Nov 17 intrusion a separate cyberattack; no source ties the two together.
notes: Needs a Bell statement saying one campaign or one actor.

claim_text: Bell Canada says an "agentic" attacker stole enterprise customer data on Nov 17
summary: Bell told CBC, the Globe and Mail and BleepingComputer that on Nov 17 an "agentic" threat actor accessed some systems, including one used to order and provision circuits, and took some enterprise customer data.
detail: Bell says the data is business contact details (names, titles, corporate emails, phone numbers, addresses), ticket titles and some network IP addresses, with no credentials, files or attachments. Bell says it contained the incident, had no customer service impact and does not know who did it. The Free Press story paraphrases the spokesperson as saying personal information of some customers was obtained, without highly sensitive details; the other outlets describe business customers' contact data. BleepingComputer first saw a customer notice from Bell's security team.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Bell gave on-record statements to three outlets, each reporting the intrusion and the data theft.
notes: Three outlets each got their own Bell statement; BleepingComputer also read a customer notice. This page does not cover the Bell Canada breach in full.

claim_text: Bell shared details with the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security and called in the RCMP
summary: Bell says it shared indicators of compromise with the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security and enterprise customers, and is working with the RCMP's cybercrime unit on the Nov 17 incident.
detail: CBC says Bell contacted the RCMP cybercrime unit; the Free Press says Bell is working with it. Neither agency was read directly.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: CBC and the Free Press each report Bell saying it involved both bodies.

claim_text: The province asked Bell MTS for a full explanation
summary: On Nov 20 a spokesperson for the province's infrastructure minister said email outages like this are unacceptable and the province expects Bell MTS to explain the cause fully and transparently.
detail: Reported by the Free Press before Bell named a cyberattack. We did not read a government release.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The Free Press quotes the ministry spokesperson.

claim_text: Bell says Bell MTS customers were among those affected by its Nov 17 data incident
summary: A Bell spokesperson told CBC on Nov 23 that customers with Bell, Bell Aliant, Bell MTS, Virgin Plus and Lucky Mobile were affected after an 'agentic threat actor' accessed some Bell internal systems on Nov 17.
detail: The statement is about customer personal information in Bell's Nov 17 incident, not about the email outage, and does not mention email. Bell did not say how many customers were affected. Bell's notice for its customers says no credit card or bank account information was impacted.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: CBC reports Bell's spokesperson naming Bell MTS among the brands whose customers were affected on Nov 17.
notes: One outlet relaying a company statement.
